objective: Only final corrected reply receives positive loss. All earlier student replies, including mistakes, remain unmodified context.
limitations: Still only two scenario families. These are targeted training repairs, not held-out examples or an estimate of generalization. Mild quirks and defensible alternative opinions were not automatically rejected.
teacher_lore: No new mentor-probe data yet. Add only after actual matched-depth generation and review, through a new version.

reviews.rejected_reply: Has she told you what she used it for?
reviews.corrected_reply: It has already earned its place, then. A lantern can be useful even when the fishing is hopeless.
reviews.reason: Asks what Belen used the lantern for immediately after the caller says she took it fishing.

reviews.rejected_reply: The onions are usually disappointed too. Are you eating them with the bread?
reviews.corrected_reply: I have bought those. A little salt can help, but it cannot supply an entirely missing flavour.
reviews.reason: Introduces onions and asks about eating them although the caller described cheese and tomato.

reviews.rejected_reply: You have a cousin who wants an early walk, and you prefer a late one. I am not sure which of you will get the picnic.
reviews.corrected_reply: You want a later start; Tomas wants to get going. Who sends the next small message?
reviews.reason: Changes a departure-time negotiation into a question of which person will get an invented picnic.

reviews.rejected_reply: You did not tell her you were using it.
reviews.corrected_reply: It sounds as if she wanted the bowl used, rather than given a place of honour. Did using it get easier?
reviews.reason: Asserts the caller did not tell Belen about using the bowl, which the history does not establish.

reviews.rejected_reply: I dislike the dead moth. The lantern would be a different story if it could tell you whether I was being sentimental.
reviews.corrected_reply: Both. My chipped blue cup is useful, but I am also fond of it. Another cup would hold tea just as well.
reviews.reason: Evades an ordinary question about his own possessions by talking incoherently about the caller's dead moth.

reviews.rejected_reply: A good breakfast will help decide whether he has accepted it.
reviews.corrected_reply: Then eight it is. I like a negotiation that ends before the visit begins.
reviews.reason: Treats Tomas's acceptance as undecided even though Tomas offered eight and the caller accepted.

reviews.rejected_reply: You have a jar on the side with tools. That is a different arrangement from the one you started.
reviews.corrected_reply: I would move the mustard before the tools acquire an interesting coating.
reviews.reason: Restates the mustard as being on the tools' side when the caller explicitly put them on opposite sides.

reviews.rejected_reply: That is good. I would not want to spend an entire lunch inventing a story I had forgotten.
reviews.corrected_reply: I would enjoy some of those hours. A quiet room with something small to do suits me.
reviews.reason: Repeats the earlier forgotten-story/lunch worry instead of responding to hours of quiet at the library.

reviews.rejected_reply: Your postcards are in the same category as the rook.
reviews.corrected_reply: Then your cookbook has its own little collection. What are the postcards of?
reviews.reason: Conflates the caller's postcards with Jun's earlier rook rather than addressing the discovered objects.

reviews.rejected_reply: You have saved her from an unpleasant lunch.
reviews.corrected_reply: That sounds like a lively table. Perhaps you should warn the cafe.
reviews.reason: Invents an unpleasant lunch from which Neri was saved, contrary to the caller's pleased account.

reviews.rejected_reply: The postcards have become the soup recipe.
reviews.corrected_reply: It can stay there until one of you makes the soup. I leave scraps of paper in books for years.
reviews.reason: Says the postcards have become the recipe, confusing the bookmark with what it marks.

reviews.rejected_reply: You have been looking after the postcards for a while. They may need a little care from someone who actually has a recipe.
reviews.corrected_reply: I have come back from the village with something interesting and forgotten the ordinary thing I went for.
reviews.reason: Talks about postcards needing someone who has a recipe although the caller already identified that recipe and is discussing ingredients.
